sources.entry: mlx-lm - Run and fine-tune large language models on Apple Silicon with MLX.

summary.one_liner: mlx-lm is a Python package for generating text, chatting, quantizing, and fine-tuning large language models on Apple silicon using the MLX framework.
summary.what_it_does: It loads MLX-compatible models from the Hugging Face Hub and runs them through command-line tools (mlx_lm.generate, mlx_lm.chat, mlx_lm.convert, mlx_lm.cache_prompt, mlx_lm.server, mlx_lm.benchmark). It provides a Python API with load, generate, stream_generate, and convert functions, plus configurable samplers and logits processors. It can quantize models and upload them to the Hugging Face Hub. The README also describes low-rank and full fine-tuning, including for quantized models, and distributed inference and fine-tuning via mx.distributed. For long contexts it offers a rotating fixed-size key-value cache, prompt caching, and a configurable prefill step size.
use_cases: Running a local LLM on a Mac for text generation
Chatting with a language model in the terminal
Quantizing a Hugging Face model to 4-bit for Apple silicon
Uploading converted MLX models to the Hugging Face Hub
Fine-tuning a language model on Apple silicon
Reusing a long cached prompt across multiple queries
notable: Runs LLMs natively on Apple silicon via the MLX framework
Single-command access to thousands of Hugging Face Hub models
Rotating key-value cache and prompt caching for long prompts
Quantize and upload models to the Hugging Face Hub from the CLI or Python
Distributed inference and fine-tuning with mx.distributed
caveats: Targets Apple silicon; the README frames it around that hardware
Large-model memory wiring requires macOS 15.0 or higher
Models large relative to RAM can run slowly; the README suggests raising the iogpu.wired_limit_mb sysctl
